rationale:
This PR teaches the transferred retained-UI-kernel surface core/view/src/yoga_layout.cpp to give a flex container's own bare text an anonymous item on the flex line in one more case than it already did. The existing behaviour -- a Label that ALSO has element children gets an anonymous text node so its text does not lay out at the same content origin as its first child -- is unchanged. What is added is the sibling case CSS also specifies: a Label with NO element children still needs that slot, because otherwise justify-content and align-items have nothing to distribute and the container's own text is painted at the content origin no matter what the container asked for. Concretely, wants_anonymous_text_box changes from `has_managed_children && has_text` to `has_text && (has_managed_children || text_alone_needs_a_slot)`.

The new case is deliberately narrow, and the two guards are the substance of this record rather than an aside. First, flex_alignment_moves_lone_item() returns false for every alignment that provably cannot displace a single item on its own line: justify-content start and space-between (which resolves to flex-start for one item), and align-items start, stretch, auto and baseline (which all leave the cross axis at the leading edge -- a lone item's own baseline is the line's maximum baseline, so baseline alignment places it exactly where flex-start would). So the default-aligned container -- the overwhelming majority of existing Labels -- takes exactly the path it took before, including the intrinsic measure-and-return. Only center, end, space-around, space-evenly, and the cross-axis center and end reach the new code. Second, text_alone_needs_a_slot additionally requires cached_line_boxes().empty(). A browser capture records each line rectangle relative to the owning element's content box, so the distribution the browser already performed is baked into that rectangle's own left/top; resolving it a second time here would offset the line by the sum of both. A captured Label therefore keeps painting from its capture and is untouched by this change.

One control-flow restructure is worth naming explicitly because it is the part a reader could mistake for a refactor. The function previously tested `if (!has_managed_children)` twice in a row -- once to install the intrinsic measure/baseline funcs, once to return -- and those are now a single block whose condition is `!has_managed_children && !wants_anonymous_text_box`. For every view that does not take the new case the condition evaluates identically and the emitted sequence is the same. For a view that does take it, the change is the intended one: the container stops measuring itself through intrinsic_width()/intrinsic_height() and instead delegates to the anonymous child that now carries the measure and baseline funcs. That is a real behaviour change for those containers and is not claimed to be equivalence-preserving; it is what the fix is.

The anonymous node is given YGNodeStyleSetFlexShrink(1.0f) because CSS gives an anonymous flex item the initial `flex: 0 1 auto`, whereas Yoga's default for a freshly created node is a shrink factor of zero. Without it a long string in a fixed-width container that used to wrap or ellipsize inside its own box would instead spill past the container. lays_out_own_children hoists the pre-existing grid/owns_child_layout test into a named local and is used to keep both of those modes out of the new case entirely; it changes no condition's value.

Limits, stated rather than glossed. This record makes no claim about the paint path: it says the slot is reserved and sized by layout, not that every widget which reads the slot draws it identically. It makes no claim about RTL or wrapping interactions beyond what the accompanying test asserts. And the alignment allow-list is an enumeration over the current FlexJustify and FlexAlign enums -- adding a new alignment value later requires revisiting flex_alignment_moves_lone_item rather than inheriting a safe default, which the switch statements surface at compile time rather than silently.

This is pulp-only. The anonymous-inline-box concept is CSS's, but the specific seam being changed -- Pulp's Label owning its own text box, the cached_line_boxes() browser-capture path, and the build_yoga_subtree control flow around intrinsic measurement -- is entirely Pulp's own shape. A Vellum-native retained UI kernel would resolve a container's bare text against whatever text and capture model it owns rather than inherit these guards. There is no named immutable Vellum framework commit to backport against, and this records no Vellum acknowledgement.
